issue.title: Move new Tearsheet React component to core
issue.body:
Let start the migration to core with new Tearsheet and identify the challenges


### Observations
In order to migrate tearsheet to core, we need to move below dependant components first

- [ ] TruncatedText
- [ ] SidePanel
- [ ] ActionSet

## Summary

Migrate `Tearsheet` (composable) from `carbon-for-ibm-products` into the Carbon core monorepo.

**c4ip export name:** `Tearsheet`
**Target status:** Stable
**Notes:** Old monolithic `Tearsheet` deprecated; new composable version already delivered in c4ip as a preview. Migrating to core as **stable**.

Parent epic: #22655

---

## Checklist

- [ ] Update prefix: replace `pkg.prefix (c4p)` with `usePrefix() (cds)`
- [ ] Update imports: migrate from `@carbon/react` to local paths
- [ ] Migrate shared utilities: move any missing utilities to `packages/react/src/internal/` first
- [ ] Rename test file: `Tearsheet.test.jsx` → `__tests__/Tearsheet-test.js`
- [ ] Update tests: fix mocks, remove ibm-products-only matchers, and ensure tests pass
- [ ] Rename stories file: `.stories.jsx` → `.stories.js`, and convert from CSF2 to CSF3
- [ ] Update stories: use `story.scss` with the decorator pattern, and remove `parameters.styles`
- [ ] Rename SCSS folder: `Tearsheet/` → `tearsheet/`
- [ ] Migrate styles: move to `packages/styles/scss/components/tearsheet/`
- [ ] Remove ibm-products-specific SCSS files: `_carbon-imports.scss`, `_index-with-carbon.scss`
- [ ] Register styles: add `@use 'tearsheet'` to `packages/styles/scss/components/_index.scss`
- [ ] Export component: add it to `packages/react/src/index.ts`
- [ ] Update index snapshot: include it in `packages/react/src/__tests__/index-test.js`
- [ ] Fix MDX docs: remove ibm-products imports and add `<Meta isTemplate />`
- [ ] Migrate relevant avt tests
- [ ] Strip out the proptypes (rely on [types](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/issues/22384))
- [ ] Migrate figma files
- [ ] Ensure open in stackblitz works

## How to verify

- Perform manual testing in v12 storybook and ensure nothing is breaking
- Ensure avts are migrated and passing
- **Verify the changes are intended:**
  - Delete the components folder from ibm-products repo
  - Copy the migrated component folder with all the migration changes back to products repo
  - Verify the changes in git source control in the IDE
  - Copy the newly generated style folder from carbon to ibm-products repo and compare styles to ensure no unintended styles have been added or removed

issue.body:
- Pull the code over from labs into core

issue.title: Feature Flags: Notify consumers of available flags
issue.body:
When consumers use a component or feature that has been improved or replaced via a feature flag, we should notify them of the change. 

### Justification

Notifying consumers of changes to the system in their development environment has many benefits:

* **Early access to enhancements**, providing their users with a better experience sooner rather than later
* **Reduced technical debt**, encouraging a controlled, phased transition without the pressure of last minute changes when a flag is turned on by default
* **Input on the system**, ensuring new features are more tailored to specific needs of consumers' teams and end users
* **Lower friction during breaking changes**, giving more time and flexibility to test and implement changes before they become mandatory
* **Opportunity to innovate**, allowing teams to experiment with new capabilities to better solve their product and end user's needs. This encourages a culture of innovation within the ecosystem by leveraging the latest tools before they're fully rolled out.
* **Competitive advantage**, as features behind flags improve the visual design, accessibility, performance, etc. This ultimately allows teams to give their end users a better experience compared to their competitors. 
* **Overall alignment with the future of the system**, reducing friction and helping teams make more informed choices about their user experience to ensure future compatibility.


Being notified will give teams the knowledge to take advantage of faster iteration, smoother upgrades, and more control over their adoption timeline. Without these messages we risk declining overall product quality by leaving enhancements on the table with little adoption. 

### Risks

* Notifications will very easily be seen as too noisy. We should really nail down how to not be a nuisance.
* ...

### Additional requirements

- [ ] Notify `unstable_FeatureFlags` users that FeatureFlags has been marked stable and they can should update their imports

issue.title: [Bug]: HeaderMenuItem in a SideNav is clipped, not truncated: the rule names cds--text-truncate-end, the item renders cds--text-truncate--end
issue.body:
### Package

@carbon/react, @carbon/styles

### Browser

Chrome

### Package version

@carbon/react 1.116.0 with @carbon/styles 1.115.0 (v11.116.0); unchanged in @carbon/react 1.117.0 with @carbon/styles 1.116.0 (v11.117.0) and on main at 2382eb9

### React version

v19.2.8

### Description

`HeaderMenuItem` wraps its children in `<span class="cds--text-truncate--end">`, with two dashes ([`packages/react/src/components/UIShell/HeaderMenuItem.tsx`, line 81](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/2382eb906571231dbb928004e6de19c3bc1177a2/packages/react/src/components/UIShell/HeaderMenuItem.tsx#L81)). Inside a `SideNav`, where `HeaderSideNavItems` shows the header's menus below the `lg` breakpoint, the side nav's stylesheet means to end that text in an ellipsis, but its selector spells the class with one dash ([`packages/styles/scss/components/ui-shell/side-nav/_side-nav.scss`, lines 363 to 367](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/2382eb906571231dbb928004e6de19c3bc1177a2/packages/styles/scss/components/ui-shell/side-nav/_side-nav.scss#L363-L367)):

```scss
a.#{$prefix}--side-nav__link > .#{$prefix}--side-nav__link-text,
.#{$prefix}--side-nav
  a.#{$prefix}--header__menu-item
  .#{$prefix}--text-truncate-end {
  @include text-overflow();
```

So the second selector never matches. A long item is not truncated: `a.cds--header__menu-item` inside the side nav is `white-space: nowrap` (line 491) and `.cds--side-nav` is `overflow: hidden` (line 34), so the text runs past the 256 px panel and is cut mid-word, with no ellipsis.

Expected: the selector names the class the component renders, `.cds--text-truncate--end`, the spelling the [Overflow content](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/overflow-content/) pattern documents for end-line truncation. That one change is enough: with the selector spelled with two dashes, the rule's own declarations (`overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, `white-space: nowrap`) end the same item in an ellipsis inside the panel.

Measured in Chromium at 375 px with `@carbon/styles/css/styles.css` 1.115.0 and the markup of step 1, the menu open:

| | the span's computed `text-overflow` | the span's width | the span's right edge | the panel's right edge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| as shipped | `clip` | 394 px | 464 px | 256 px |
| the selector with two dashes | `ellipsis` | 168 px | 238 px | 256 px |

### Reproduction/example

https://react.carbondesignsystem.com/?path=/story/components-ui-shell-sidenav--side-nav-rail-w-header renders `HeaderMenuItem`s inside the side nav below 1056 px. Its items are short, so nothing is cut there, but each item's span carries `cds--text-truncate--end` and no rule of the stylesheet matches it. The steps below use a long item.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Render this in a window narrower than 1056 px, 375 px for one:

```jsx
<Header aria-label="Product">
  <HeaderMenuButton aria-label="Close menu" isActive aria-expanded onClick={() => {}} />
  <HeaderName href="#" prefix="">
    Product
  </HeaderName>
  <SideNav aria-label="Side navigation" expanded>
    <SideNavItems>
      <HeaderSideNavItems>
        <HeaderMenu aria-label="Organizations" menuLinkName="Organizations">
          <HeaderMenuItem href="#">
            Distribuidora Ibérica de Artículos Ópticos y Fotográficos SL
          </HeaderMenuItem>
        </HeaderMenu>
      </HeaderSideNavItems>
    </SideNavItems>
  </SideNav>
</Header>
```

2. Open the "Organizations" menu in the side nav.
3. Inspect the item's `<span class="cds--text-truncate--end">`: its computed `text-overflow` is `clip`, and the name is cut at the panel's edge with no ellipsis.
4. In the browser's devtools, change the selector `.cds--side-nav a.cds--header__menu-item .cds--text-truncate-end` to end in `.cds--text-truncate--end`: the item ends in an ellipsis inside the panel.

### Suggested Severity

Medium (Severity 3) = User can complete task, and/or has a workaround within the user experience of a given component.

### Project name

Ready for Commerce

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct
- [x] I checked the current issues for duplicate problems

issue.title: Migrate `TagOverflow` from ibm-products to `@carbon/react`
issue.body:
## Summary

Migrate `TagOverflow` from `carbon-for-ibm-products` into the Carbon core monorepo.

**c4ip export name:** `TagOverflow`
**Target status:** Stable (TBC — see open question below)
**Notes:** Functions as a utility rather than a standalone component. Originally intended to replace `TagSet` with greater flexibility (supporting avatars, icons, and other non-tag content). Similar functionality can be achieved with overflow utilities, but those require more boilerplate — which is why migrating `TagOverflow` is favoured. Decision to be confirmed before v12 exports are uncommented.

> ⚠️ **Open question:** Final inclusion decision required before v12 exports are uncommented. See [ADR 0007](../docs/decisions/0007-ibm-products-to-core-migration.md).

Parent epic: #22655

---

## Steps

1. Identify any shared utilities used by the component being migrated.
   * If such utilities exist, migrate them first.
   * In most cases, verify whether they already exist in Carbon core before creating new ones.
2. Copy the component folder into:
   `src/components/`
3. Copy the associated styles into the styles package:
   `packages/styles/`
4. Copy any existing AVT (end-to-end) test files and Figma Code Connect files, if present.
5. Download and run the [migration prompt](https://github.com/amal-k-joy/carbon/blob/testMigrationPrompt/docs/guides/ibm-products-to-carbon-core-migration.md) with the target component name.
6. Example:
   Migrate the `TagOverflow` component that has already been copied into the repository, using:
   `docs/guides/ibm-products-to-carbon-core-migration.md`

---

## Checklist

- [ ] Confirm inclusion decision before uncommenting exports for v12
- [ ] Update prefix: replace `pkg.prefix (c4p)` with `usePrefix() (cds)`
- [ ] Update imports: migrate from `@carbon/react` to local paths
- [ ] Migrate shared utilities: move any missing utilities to `packages/react/src/internal/` first
- [ ] Rename test file: `TagOverflow.test.jsx` → `__tests__/TagOverflow-test.js`
- [ ] Update tests: fix mocks, remove ibm-products-only matchers, and ensure tests pass
- [ ] Rename stories file: `.stories.jsx` → `.stories.js`, and convert from CSF2 to CSF3
- [ ] Update stories: use `story.scss` with the decorator pattern, and remove `parameters.styles`
- [ ] Rename SCSS folder: `TagOverflow/` → `tag-overflow/`
- [ ] Migrate styles: move to `packages/styles/scss/components/tag-overflow/`

## How to verify

issue.title: [Feature Request]: Make $min-inline-button-size configurable in @carbon/styles button component
[Feature Request]: Make it possible for SideNavLink and SideNavMenuItem components to render buttons
issue.body: > [!NOTE] > This PR https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/pull/22342 handles React. However, we still need to implement the same changes for Web Components, so this issue is open until we get `Web Components` done. ### The problem At the moment, if you want to create a sidebar navigation, you would import the components and render menu items as `SideNavLink` or `SideNavMenu` with a nested `SideNavMenuItem`. The code in this case looks something like this: ``` This is a link and it renders well ``` It works well, if those are links, meaning, if you pass it the `href` prop. In that the HTML is the following: ``` This is a link and it renders well ``` However, not in all the cases the sidebar navigation menu item is a link. Sometimes it can be a button performing an action. For example, a button opening a modal with information like current version of the software or showing internal release notes. In that case you don't want to pass an `href` prop and you want to pass the `onClick` event handler instead. The component in that case looks like: ``` { // a proper action would live here console.log('I should open a modal'); }} > This is a button that opens a modal. It renders as a link without the cursor pointer, since the href prop is missing ``` The HTML looks the following way in that case: ``` This is a button that opens a modal. It renders as a link without the cursor pointer, since the href prop is missing ``` It has 2 problems: 1. It is semantically incorrect, since it is a button 2. It is missing a cursor pointer Here is a StackBlitz showing the issue: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-rd2s5bph?file=src%2FApp.jsx I would also upload the video, but the limit of 10mb doesn't allow me to do that. ### The solution 1. `SideNavMenuItem` component with no `href` prop and `onClick` prop should render a button that has the same styling as the link 2. As far as I understand, `SideNavMenuItem` has to be nested within a `SideNavMenu` component, which you cannot always do. If you want a button to be on top level of a menu, you have to use the `SideNavLink` component. In that case `SideNavLink` should also render a button, just like in point 1. 3. All of these components should have the same styles as the link component would have ### Examples _No response_ ### Application/PAL Instana ### Business priority Low Priority = release date is not dependent on fix or not upcoming ### Available extra resources _No response_ ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/blob/f555616971a03fd454c0f4daea184adf41fff05b/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

issue.title: Migrate `NotificationsPanel` web component from ibm-products to `@carbon/web-components`
issue.body:
## Summary

Migrate the `NotificationsPanel` web component from `carbon-for-ibm-products` into the Carbon core monorepo as part of the selective component migration tracked in the parent epic.

**Custom element tag:** `cds-notification-panel`
**Source:** [`ibm-products-web-components/src/components/notification-panel`](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/ibm-products/tree/main/packages/ibm-products-web-components/src/components/notification-panel)
**Target:** `packages/web-components/src/components/notification-panel/`
**Target status:** Stable
**Notes:** Might need to be made more composable in the future (post-v12). React counterpart: #22924.

**React counterpart:** #22924

Parent epic: #22794

---

## Checklist

- [ ] LitElement class (`notification-panel.ts`) — `@customElement`, `@property`, `@state` decorators; `prefix` from `../../globals/settings`; `carbonElement` decorator; no ibm-products utilities
- [ ] `index.ts` — registers the custom element only
- [ ] Export added to `packages/web-components/src/index.ts`
- [ ] Component styles (`notification-panel.scss`) — scoped to `:host(cds-notification-panel)`; uses `@carbon/styles` tokens; **not** added to `packages/styles/scss/components/_index.scss`
- [ ] Stories (`notification-panel.stories.ts`) — CSF3, `const meta = { ... }; export default meta`
- [ ] MDX docs page (`notification-panel.mdx`) — usage examples, `<ArgTypes of="cds-notification-panel" />`
- [ ] Unit tests (`__tests__/notification-panel-test.js`) — `@open-wc/testing`, shadow DOM queries, `await el.updateComplete`
- [ ] All lint, type-check, and test checks pass

## How to verify

- Perform manual testing in v12 Storybook
- Confirm `cds-notification-panel` is exported from `@carbon/web-components`
- Verify parity with the React `NotificationsPanel` component (#22924)
- **Verify the migration is complete:**
  - Delete the component from the ibm-products-web-components repo
  - Copy the migrated folder back and verify the diff in git source control
  - Compare styles to ensure no unintended changes were introduced
